approximation_interface.description: Piecewise linear log-sum-exp approximation adapted for NITI's int8 matrix operations and block scaling scheme

inputs.a_scaled: int8 - log value a scaled by layer-specific scale factor s_a
inputs.b_scaled: int8 - log value b scaled by layer-specific scale factor s_b
inputs.scale_a: float - actual scale factor for a (power of two, from block scaling)
inputs.scale_b: float - actual scale factor for b (power of two, from block scaling)

output.result_scaled: int8 - approximation of log(exp(a) + exp(b)) scaled appropriately for subsequent operations
output.output_scale: float - scale factor to apply to result_scaled to get actual log value

parameters.segments: Precomputed array of {z_left, z_right, slope, intercept} for softplus(z) approximation

data_flow: 1. NITI stores log probabilities as int8 values scaled by layer-specific factors (powers of two)
2. For log-sum-exp, retrieve the two scaled int8 values and their respective scale factors
3. Convert to actual log values: a_log = a_scaled * scale_a, b_log = b_scaled * scale_b
4. Ensure a_log >= b_log (swap if needed, remembering to swap scales too)
7. Look up segment index: seg_idx = int((z - Z_MIN) / (Z_MAX - Z_MIN) * NUM_SEGMENTS)
8. Compute approximation: log1p_exp_z ≈ slope[seg_idx] * z + intercept[seg_idx]
9. Result in log domain: result_log = a_log + log1p_exp_z
10. Convert result_log back to int8 format for NITI: result_scaled = round(result_log / output_scale)
11. Determine output_scale appropriately (typically max(scale_a, scale_b) or layer-specific)
niti_specific_adaptations: The approximation works on the actual log values (float) derived from scaled integers
The block scaling scheme's power-of-two scales enable efficient conversion (bit shifts)
The clamping to [-10,0] aligns with NITI's dynamic range for log probabilities
Only multiplication, addition, and comparison are used - all efficient in int8/int32 arithmetic
The segment lookup table (40 entries) is small enough for on-chip storage

integration_requirements: Must maintain numerical stability in log domain
Input clamping to [-10, 0] must be preserved
Should work with NITI's block scaling scheme (powers-of-two scaling factors)
Only multiplication, addition, and comparison operations should be used in the core approximation
Input and output should remain compatible with NITI's int8 representation
The approximation should not break the integer-only property of NITI

estimated_resource_usage.lookup_table: 40 segments × (slope + intercept) = 80 values (can be int8 or int16)
estimated_resource_usage.computation: Approx 5-10 integer operations per log-add-exp (multiply, add, compare)
estimated_resource_usage.precision: Designed to match 4.4 fixed-point format (4 integer, 4 fractional bits) for log values in [-10,0]

test_cases_niti.description: Symmetric case: log(exp(x) + exp(x)) = x + log(2)
